name: CT-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jim Himes with large financial advantage ($2.5M cash vs $41K)
No polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: Himes holds a heavily Democratic seat, a massive fundraising edge, and no serious outside spending against him, while challenger Goldstein has raised almost nothing. Markets price this near-certain for Democrats, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 22 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Himes or a major national Republican wave environment could narrow the margin, though a seat this blue is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Himes seeks another term in a Connecticut district that leans Democratic by about 13 points, and he enters with a commanding financial position: roughly $2.5 million on hand after raising nearly $1.4 million, against about $41,000 for Republican Michael Goldstein. No outside groups are spending against Himes, and an independent candidate is on the ballot but has shown no measurable support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which point the same way. Prediction markets give Himes roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and the expected margin sits in the low twenties.
